source.request: I want to make a page about me

title: A page about me
summary: Build a one-page website with your name, a short intro and a list of things you like, then add a splash of colour.
outcome: A web page about you that opens in any browser.
learns: the parts of an HTML page
changing colours and fonts with CSS

files.content:
Hi, I'm Sam

I'm learning to make websites.

This page is all about me.

Things I like

  • Drawing
  • Basketball
  • Cooking

steps.title: Open VS Code
steps.instruction: Stride opens VS Code, where you'll write your page.
steps.why: VS Code is where you type code and see mistakes underlined.
hints: Stride is opening VS Code for you.
Look for the VS Code window.
If it didn't open, open it from your Applications folder.

steps.title: The page skeleton
steps.instruction: In index.html, type the basic parts every web page has: the doctype, <html>, <head> with a <title>, and an empty <body>.
steps.why: Browsers need this skeleton to know it's a web page.
hints: Inside <html>, put a <head> first, then a <body>.

concept.title: The parts of an HTML page
concept.explain: The <head> holds facts about the page, like its title, and the <body> holds everything people see.
concept.imageQuery: html page structure head body diagram

steps.title: Say hi
steps.instruction: Inside <body>, add a big heading with your name and two short paragraphs about you.
steps.why: The heading is the first thing visitors read.
steps.expected:
Hi, I'm Sam

I'm learning to make websites.

This page is all about me.
hints: A big heading uses the <h1> tag.

Put the

and both

lines between and .

steps.title: Things you like
steps.instruction: Under your paragraphs, add a smaller heading and a list of 3 things you like.
steps.why: Lists keep related things together and easy to scan.
hints: A bullet list uses <ul>, and each item is an <li>.

concept.title: Lists
concept.explain: A <ul> makes a bullet list, and each thing in it goes inside its own <li> (list item).

steps.title: Finish the head
steps.instruction: In the <head>, under the <title>, add a short description of the page, a line that makes it fit phone screens, and a <link> that points to style.css.
steps.why: This tells the page where its colours and fonts live.
steps.expected:
<meta name="description" content="A page about me, Sam.">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
hints: Styles are connected with a <link> tag in the <head>.
The <link> needs rel="stylesheet" and an href.

concept.title: Linking CSS
concept.explain: A <link> in the <head> connects your page to a CSS file, which says how the page looks.

steps.title: Add some colour
steps.instruction: In style.css, give the page a clean font and some space, and make your heading tomato red.
steps.why: A few lines of CSS make the page feel like yours.
hints: CSS rules look like: selector { property: value; }
Write a rule for h1 that sets color.

quiz.question: Which tag connects a CSS file to your page?
quiz.explain: <link rel="stylesheet"> loads a separate CSS file.
